chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
In the bequest of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to Ali (peace be upon him), he said: 'O Ali, I bequeath to you regarding yourself certain qualities, so preserve them from me.'

Then he said: 'O Allah, support him. As for the first, it is truthfulness, and do not let a lie come out of your mouth ever. And the second is piety (al-wara'), and do not be audacious in treachery ever. And the third is fear of Allah, Mighty is His Mention, as if you see Him. And the fourth is much weeping from the fear of Allah; a thousand houses will be built for you in Paradise for every tear. And the fifth is spending your wealth and your blood for the sake of your Religion. And the sixth is adhering to my Sunnah in my Prayer, my Fasting, and my Charity.'

As for the Prayer, it is fifty Rakaat. And as for the Fasting, it is three days in the month: Thursday in the first part, Wednesday in the middle, and Thursday in the last part. And as for the Charity, it is your utmost effort, to the point that you say 'I have been excessive,' yet you have not been excessive.

And upon you is the Night Prayer, and upon you is the Noon Prayer, and upon you is the Noon Prayer, and upon you is the Noon Prayer. And upon you is reciting the Quran in every condition. And upon you is raising your hands in your Prayer and turning them. And upon you is using the Siwak at every ablution. And upon you is adopting good morals and avoiding bad morals; if you do not do so, do not blame anyone but yourself.
ai.seo_question: What are the six qualities the Prophet bequeathed to Imam Ali in his will?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s specific bequest to Imam Ali, emphasizing six core virtues: truthfulness, piety, God-consciousness, weeping in prayer, and self-sacrifice for the faith. It provides unique jurisprudential details, such as the specific days for monthly fasting and the emphasis on the 'Prayer of Midday' (Salat al-Zawal), while linking moral excellence directly to ritual practice. This narration underscores the Shia tradition of integrating ethical conduct with precise ritual observance as a path to spiritual elevation.
